design_detail: Critical assessment comparing dopamine-system findings in methamphetamine users (imaging, post-mortem) with Parkinson's disease, asking whether 'damage' is the right description.
can_establish: Whether the pattern and magnitude of dopamine marker changes in users are consistent with neuronal loss as seen in Parkinson's disease.

sample.selection_effects: Author group includes the senior author of a registry study on Parkinson's risk; see funding/interests.

interpretation_gap.results_show: The authors argue that DAT and dopamine reductions in users are modest relative to Parkinson's disease, partly reversible, and compatible with regulation rather than terminal loss, while not excluding some loss; and that the epidemiological Parkinson's signal deserves attention.
interpretation_gap.claimed: Consistent with content [to be extracted from PDF]

replication.where_it_stands: The most careful published treatment of the 'damage' question; central to the debate box.

funding.affiliations_note: Callaghan and Kish are authors of the 2012 Parkinson's registry study (callaghan_2012).

what_would_settle_it: Post-mortem studies with multiple terminal markers; longitudinal imaging.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Narrative; used for its arguments and its summary of post-mortem evidence, not as a synthesis.
